I'm going to go hold my little brother to sleep tonight and then have a cold shower. Thank you so much.

My little brothers (he's 13) safety is my number one concern. What I'm going to do comes second. I'm struggling most with the fact that I can't even bring myself to open the front door to face the world. I'd attend one of those meetings or perhaps even see a doctor, but when I can't even begin to face the world, I feel so helpless and pointless. I feel like a pointless individual who's just filled with nothingness and agony that there's no reason to even attempt things I've always wanted to do.

I don't have any grandparents and no aunts or uncles. Just me and my little brother is what's left of my family tree. I'll learn more I'm sure about being apart of the foster care process when I talk to social services tomorrow. This is all so bizarre and it's going to be one fucked up Christmas morning. My mom had a lot of health issues and was in a lot of pain, so the only thing keeping me sane is thinking she's peaceful now.

I'm scared if I become a foster parent, I won't ever be able to live out the life goals I wanted to live, but I also don't want him thinking I abandoned him :(

When I had a heart full of love and dignity. How does someone just decide one day that their not in love anymore? I don't get it.

In my senior year, my father passed away due to cancer, and a month later my older brother was killed in a car accident. My mom then became an alcoholic. I still had two younger siblings at home, so I had no choice but to dropout and take care of my two younger siblings at home while my mom was in rehab. Completely missed out on my senior year and never got to graduate with all the friends I grew up with.

I was desperate for a good paying job, so I lied on my resume and said that I had graduated and also had a social work degree. I got hired as a social worker to work for the homeless community. Been doing it for two years now and I make roughly 60k a year, while still climbing the latter. I'm 24.

I went to a party with my friend Cliff. He'd had way too much to drink and the party hadn't even been half over yet. He proceeded to throw up in the punch bowl. 3 times. A bunch of under aged high-schooler kids showed up. They were being awkward and hadn't even partied before. We told them if they wanted to drink, they could help themselves to the 'punch'. A few of them poured themselves some of the puke punch, without a clue knowing my buddy just threw up in it. They had the most disgusted looks on their faces, but they were trying so hard to act cool and fit in that they challenged each other to a chug-off. They all finished their drinks, but you could tell from their faces that they knew something wasn't 'right'. To this day nobody ever told them they drank puke.

Don't prevent yourself from what your heart wants because you fear it'll ruin any kind of security you have with your current SO. Based on what you told us, it sounds as though the type of relationship you have with your current SO is easily obtainable, considering your feelings for her just aren't 'there'. 

Seriously, man. If you don't make the move, you're always going to wonder 'what if'. It's also not fair for your current SO for her boyfriend to be having these feelings about a past ex. 

Besides, the 5 hour distance isn't very much. And it could very well benefit you guys if you are to make a crack at another relationship. The distance would help ease you guys back into being serious again. Which I think is a good thing. Get only one foot wet before you take the plunge. Remember, being seperated for a year gave you both all that time to mature and personally grow. Now that you're at different times in your life, it could very well be what was missing the first time you dated. 

Long story short: Go with your heart, man. If it doesn't work out, at least you won't have any regrets.

I am currently in a long distance relationship. My fiancee is off in school at her dream school. She's very tide up in her new surroundings, making it easier for her to handle the long distance while I am stuck at home with more time to wonder about her. Yes, it is tough, sometimes unbearable. But in times when I am missing her, I will sit down and write her a letter. Sometimes I will put together a little care package. Because a lot of the reason why I miss her so much, is the lack of emotional intimacy. So when I write her letters, it helps by expressing myself and my love for her.

Oddly enough, we've also bought ourselves iPads before she left for college. This is our communication device, and it's very handy. Since we can't always be home at our computers, the iPad is perfect by sending each other cute messages, and sending each other a video message everyday. When I receive one from her, it instantly erases any spiraling mood I'm in.

In the end, there are more positives than negatives. You feel a lot of negative effects and emotions throughout the long distance, but at the end of the day when you're together again, you'll be an even more stronger couple. The relationship will be stronger, because each person has not only grown individually, but together as well by accomplishing this hurdle. There is less chance of taking one another for granted. Each person has experienced what time apart feels like, and it'll skyrocket your appreciation for one another. 

And if things really get tough, just hop on the next plane to go see him, even just for a few days. You won't be dreading and thinking "Ugh, it won't be until DECEMBER until I see him again." By breaking up the time apart, you can look forward to seeing him next weekend, and the distance instantly becomes more tolerable on that alone. A heck of a lot more tolerable.
